requirement.evidence: The law prohibits the sale or use of such algorithmic devices and allows a tenant or the City Attorney to bring a civil action if they believe an entity is in violation of the law.
requirement.note: Definition covers software analyzing nonpublic competitor rental data for rent recommendations; occupancy management is in the law's description.

key_value.evidence: Each month of use for each affected dwelling unit may constitute a separate violation, and tenants may seek damages, injunctive relief, and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation. S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C(b) and (d).
key_value.note: D002 supports the $1,000 per violation, per unit per month.

effective_date.evidence: adding Section 37.10C to the Rent Ordinance went into effect on October 14, 2024.

status.evidence: Gomez v. Greystar Management Services LLC in the Northern District of California, alleging that Greystar violated San Francisco Administrative Code § 37.10C through its alleged use of RealPage and Yardi products.
status.note: Document presents the ordinance as current law, being enforced in 2026.

coverage.note: Coverage is empty on the card.

citation.note: Section 37.10C is also cited in D081.
